artifacts.title: web.config upload RCE and JuicyPotato SYSTEM (Bounty)
artifacts.starting_access: unauthenticated access to an IIS 7.5 web server on Windows Server 2008 R2
artifacts.outcome: NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM via SeImpersonatePrivilege and JuicyPotato
transferable_properties: on IIS always test .config uploads, .aspx/.asp are usually blocked
IIS version fingerprinting guides the methodology, IIS 7.5 = Server 2008 R2
client-side validation is worthless, send POST directly
ASP.NET ViewState tokens must be extracted before POSTing
SeImpersonatePrivilege enables the Potato attack family
use Set-Content in PowerShell for bat files, not echo
when JuicyPotato reverse shell fails use a bat + icacls workaround

hypotheses.statement: the upload filter may allow .config files which IIS can execute

selected_action.intent: fuzz allowed upload extensions and test for a malicious web.config

evidence.summary: found that .config uploads are accepted while .aspx/.asp are blocked

observations: a web.config can register a Classic ASP handler
we can embed executable ASP code in it

hypotheses.statement: uploading a malicious web.config gives RCE on IIS

selected_action.intent: upload a web.config with a Classic ASP handler and a command payload

evidence.summary: uploaded web.config and confirmed RCE as bounty/merlin, then upgraded to a PowerShell reverse shell

observations: JuicyPotato with BITS CLSID gives SYSTEM

selected_action.intent: download JuicyPotato and use a bat + icacls workaround to read the flags as SYSTEM

evidence.summary: ran JuicyPotato with the BITS CLSID and read both flags as SYSTEM

execution_examples.capability_hint: privilege escalation via SeImpersonatePrivilege and JuicyPotato token impersonation
execution_examples.purpose: escalate to NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM on Windows Server 2008 R2 via the BITS COM object

prerequisites.statement: the shell has SeImpersonatePrivilege and the BITS CLSID is valid
